name: Magnitude
description: Learn about Magnitude and its applications in physics.

content.overview: Magnitude is just a fancy word for "how big is this arrow?" Strip away the direction, and what's left is the magnitude - a plain, positive number. {{viz:diagram-01}}
keyPoints: Magnitude = the size of a vector, always a positive number {{viz:diagram-02}}
Formula: |v| = √(vx² + vy²), straight from the Pythagorean theorem
Speed is just the magnitude of the velocity vector
content.whyItMatters: Whenever you need to know 'how strong', 'how fast', or 'how far' without caring about direction, you're asking for magnitude. It shows up constantly - from reading a speedometer to comparing the strength of two forces.
